interest: This file is particularly interesting to diplomatic, economic, and illicit trade historians because it reveals how routine monitoring of foreign capital investment and commercial concessions quickly intersected with international narcotics intelligence. While formally filed under capital investment in Iran (894.503191), the State Department's primary concern shifted to Japan's procurement of Persian raw opium to supply its domestic opium monopoly and morphine manufacturers. Moreover, the docket sheet provides valuable insight into Department of State record-keeping practices, showing the cross-referencing and transfer of economic files to the specialized narcotics surveillance classification (891.114) and close liaison with the Treasury Department.
overview: This file consists of a single-page Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet covering records from April to July 1931 filed under decimal file 894.503191 (concerning Japanese capital investment in Persia/Iran). The entries document diplomatic correspondence involving the American Legation in Tehran (Minister Charles C. Hart), the American Embassy in Tokyo (Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville), the Department of State's geographic divisions (FE, NE, EA), and the Treasury Department. Prompted by Persian press reports regarding the encouragement of Japanese capital investments, the State Department initiated inquiries regarding Japanese commercial involvement in Persian opium transactions. Subsequent reporting from Tokyo revealed that the Japanese opium monopoly and manufacturers of morphine and its salts had long purchased supplies from Persia. The docket sheet records the transmission of these reports between posts and departments, noting that the substantive correspondence was cross-referenced and transferred to decimal file 891.114 (Narcotics).

subfiles.about: A Department of State docket list cataloguing incoming and outgoing diplomatic correspondence between April and July 1931 regarding Japanese investment and opium procurement in Persia.
subfiles.summary: This administrative docket sheet records despatches, departmental instructions, and interdepartmental communications concerning Japanese capital investment and commercial activities in Persia from April 16 to July 22, 1931. It indexes Despatch No. 529 from Minister Charles C. Hart in Tehran reporting Persian press accounts of Japanese capital investment, along with Department instructions transmitting copies to the Treasury Department and the Embassy in Tokyo while requesting further information on opium transactions. It also records Despatch No. 268 from Chargé Edwin L. Neville in Tokyo describing the Japanese opium monopoly and morphine manufacturers purchasing supplies from Persia, noting that the substantive files were cross-referenced to decimal file 891.114 (Narcotics).
